title: Brightgate Financial - Data residency & compliance discovery
next_steps: Send SOC 2 + HIPAA + GDPR compliance pack and network diagram
Share proposed Dedicated capacity sizing and pricing
Schedule a technical deep-dive with infra team (SE-led) for pilot details
Provide example audit log retention config and masking options
action_items: Alex Turner: Email compliance pack and pricing by 2026-04-01
Priya Shah: Schedule SE deep-dive and share benchmark plan by 2026-04-03
Ethan Cole: Share current data flow diagram and list of external integrations by 2026-04-02
summary: Initial discovery focused on data residency and compliance requirements for a potential deployment of Redwood (hosted vs dedicated vs private). Brightgate has strict logging and residency constraints driven by financial regulators; primary concerns were audit logs, KMS integration, SSO/SAML, and ability to keep data fully within their EU/UK regions or on-prem. Agreed next steps: send compliance docs, propose Dedicated sizing/pricing, and schedule SE-led pilot planning.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
transcript: [00:00] Alex Turner: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. I'm Alex, AE at Redwood Inference. With me is Priya, our solutions engineer.
[00:10] Marcus Liu: Morning. Marcus here, CTO at Brightgate. Sofia from compliance and Ethan from infra are on too.
[00:15] Sofia Ramirez: Hi all.
[00:22] Priya Shah: Quick agenda, we'll run a short discovery on your requirements, talk data residency, security controls, then map Redwood hosting options to those needs. Sound good?
[00:35] Lena Park: Yep, that's the list. We have about an hour.
[00:42] Alex Turner: Great. Marcus can you start with current stack and what you're trying to solve with LLMs?

[00:50] Marcus Liu: Sure. We're building a customer support assistant and an internal compliance triage tool. We run mostly in AWS eu-west-1, some UK accounts. We need to ensure customer PII never leaves EU/UK and that audit logs are retained for seven years per our regulator. Latency requirements are modest for async support, but for some internal tools low latency is desired. We're evaluating Redwood for pilot and then a production rollout if it meets compliance.

[01:20] Alex Turner: Thanks. On residency, we support three deployment modes — hosted (multi-region), Dedicated reserved pools, and Private (VPC/on-prem). For strict residency you typically look at Dedicated or Private. Quick question: do you require customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM)?

[01:40] Sofia Ramirez: Yes, we need customer-owned keys; we can't have plaintext data decryptable by vendor staff. Also, we need proof that logs don't contain full PII and that any retained logs can be masked or redacted. GDPR DPIA concerns here too.

[02:05] Priya Shah: Understood. For Dedicated we offer KMS integration so keys never leave your KMS and logs are segregated per-customer. For Private on-prem we can run the control plane in your VPC or air-gapped environment, which is the strongest guarantee but has more ops work.

[02:30] Ethan Cole: If we go Dedicated, do we still have control over egress? We have partners in the US; some requests might need to call external systems but we want to avoid model payloads leaving region.

[02:45] Priya Shah: You can configure routing policies — keep requests in eu-west-1/uk regions; fallbacks only to other variants if you allow it. We can pin a model version and region. If you require zero egress, Private is recommended.
[03:05] Marcus Liu: What's the difference in cost and performance between Dedicated and Private? We're sensitive to both.

[03:12] Alex Turner: Dedicated is reserved infra in our cloud with predictable throughput and lower ops overhead — good middle ground. Private (VPC/or on-prem) increases ops and initial setup but gives max control and potentially lower long-run egress costs depending on infra. We'll send a sizing/pricing sheet in the follow-up.
[03:36] Sofia Ramirez: Compliance question — SOC 2 and HIPAA. We handle some health-adjacent data. Do you have BAAs and a SOC 2 Type II report?

[03:46] Priya Shah: Yes, we have SOC 2 Type II and a BAA offering for HIPAA covered workloads. We'll share copies. For HIPAA we recommend Dedicated or Private and encryption-in-transit and at-rest with customer KMS.
[04:05] Lena Park: On logging — we need to limit what's logged. Can we disable full request/response logging and only retain metadata and masked extracts?

[04:15] Priya Shah: Yes, we support configurable logging levels. By default we log request IDs, timestamps, model used, and token counts. We can disable full-text logging or apply automatic redaction of PII via built-in masking rules or customer-provided regex lists.
[04:40] Marcus Liu: How does that interact with debugging if something goes wrong? We still need traceability for incidents.
[04:46] Alex Turner: You can enable verbose logs for a narrow time window or specific request IDs for debugging; logs can be exported to your S3 or SIEM with retention policies under your control.
[04:58] Ethan Cole: Does Redwood store KV cache or any model state with customer data on shared storage? We need to be sure no unencrypted caches leak.

[05:08] Priya Shah: KV caches are in-memory on the serving nodes; for Dedicated they're per-customer and ephemeral, and for Private they live in your environment. We avoid writing unencrypted caches to shared disk; any persisted caches are encrypted and can be backed by your KMS.
[05:28] Sofia Ramirez: GDPR: we need data subject rights, deletion of personal data, and logs proving deletion. How do you handle deletion across different modes?

[05:37] Priya Shah: For Hosted we have deletion APIs and a documented retention process but you'd need to trust the provider. For Dedicated we can configure retention windows and provide deletion confirmations and audit logs. Private gives you full control to run deletion processes in your environment.
[05:58] Marcus Liu: What about access controls? SSO, RBAC, and audit trails?

[06:04] Alex Turner: We support SAML SSO, SCIM for provisioning, and fine-grained RBAC in the console. All admin actions are logged and can be exported. We'll include the RBAC matrix in the deck we send.
[06:20] Lena Park: Any regulatory approvals needed? ISO, PCI, anything special?

[06:26] Priya Shah: We maintain SOC 2 and are working on ISO 27001; PCI is not currently in-scope for platform-managed cardholder data, but we can document network segmentation options. We'll surface any gaps relevant to Brightgate's specific audits.
[06:42] Marcus Liu: For the pilot, we want to run some benchmarks — latency and throughput with our prompts and a sample anonymized dataset. Can you run that in our region with Dedicated nodes?

[06:52] Priya Shah: Yes, we can provision a small Dedicated pool in eu-west-1 for a time-boxed pilot. We'll need a workload spec, expected qps, and sequence lengths. We can also run privacy-preserving benchmarks if you provide sanitized data or synthetic equivalents.
[07:10] Ethan Cole: Network connectivity — do you support private link / VPC peering? We want no public internet traffic for inference calls.
[07:18] Priya Shah: We support AWS PrivateLink, VPC peering, and site-to-site VPN for Private and Dedicated. Hosted can be used via API with IP allowlists but isn't fully private.
[07:30] Sofia Ramirez: Audit logs retention — we need seven years. Is that feasible and how is cost handled?

[07:36] Alex Turner: We can push audit logs to your S3 with lifecycle policies you control; retention cost would be your S3 cost in that case. We can also offer managed retention for an additional fee.
[07:48] Marcus Liu: Data residency for training/updates — are any customer inputs ever used to fine-tune shared models?

[07:55] Priya Shah: No. By default we don't use customer data for model fine-tuning. We can sign contractual language to that effect. For customers who want private fine-tuning, that's available in Dedicated/Private with explicit controls.

[08:10] Lena Park: Is it possible to have a hybrid model — most customer traffic stays in EU, but during peak we burst to other regions? Our compliance team might allow controlled bursts with consent.

[08:20] Alex Turner: Yes, we support routing policies and burst capacity. For regulated workloads we usually avoid cross-border bursts unless contractually allowed; we can configure explicit fallback rules that require an allowlist.
[08:34] Marcus Liu: What about data sovereignty in the UK post-Brexit — do you have explicit UK region hosting?
[08:40] Priya Shah: We support deployments in AWS eu-west-2 (London) and can pin assets there for Dedicated. Private on-prem or VPC in a UK region is also possible.
[08:52] Sofia Ramirez: Can you provide an example DPIA or compliance mapping for GDPR articles and our controls?
[08:58] Alex Turner: We'll include a GDPR mapping matrix in the pack. It will map data flows, roles, processors/sub-processors, retention, and deletion procedures.
[09:10] Ethan Cole: One technical nit — how do you handle model outputs that might contain customer PII in free text? We need at-rest masking and optional output filters.

[09:20] Priya Shah: We have response filters and post-processing hooks. You can run automatic PII detectors that redact or replace sensitive tokens before storing or returning outputs. For ultimate control, run those filters in your Private environment.
[09:38] Marcus Liu: For the pilot we'd like to test both chat generation and embeddings for search. Are embeddings stored, and if so can they be encrypted and isolated?
[09:48] Priya Shah: Embeddings can be stored in customer-owned stores or in Redwood's Dedicated isolated stores encrypted with your KMS. Retrieval and vector store integration are configurable.
[09:58] Lena Park: Any configured limits on searchable content? We want to ensure compliance reviews don't accidentally expose old sensitive documents.
[10:05] Priya Shah: We can implement per-index access controls and masking at ingestion. Also support deletion APIs to remove vectors/documents on request.
[10:18] Sofia Ramirez: Contractually we need subprocessor disclosures. Who are your cloud providers and any third-party services involved?

[10:25] Alex Turner: Primary infra providers are AWS and GCP depending on region; we use third-party monitoring and observability tools — we'll provide a full subprocessor list in the compliance pack.
[10:36] Marcus Liu: Is there a mechanism to prove chain of custody for logs? Our auditors ask for immutable logs.
[10:41] Priya Shah: We can export logs to your immutable storage with WORM policies in S3 or to your SIEM. We also provide signed audit snapshots for key events if needed.
[10:56] Ethan Cole: What are typical lead times to get Dedicated infra up in a region?
[11:01] Alex Turner: Usually 2-4 weeks for small Dedicated pools, depending on capacity. Private/on-prem can take longer due to networking/infra setup.
[11:12] Marcus Liu: For the POC, what's the recommended minimal configuration? We want representative perf and security.
[11:18] Priya Shah: A small Dedicated pool (2 nodes) in your region, sample sanitized dataset, and our benchmark harness. We'll instrument logging levels and masking rules for the pilot.
[11:30] Lena Park: Will you provide support during the pilot — a named SE and SLA timeframe for incidents?
[11:35] Alex Turner: Yes, pilot includes SE support. For production we offer different SLA tiers; Dedicated customers can get higher SLA and faster response times.
[11:45] Marcus Liu: A few questions from Sofia — retention of monitoring telemetry vs audit logs, and separation between them.
[11:52] Sofia Ramirez: We want monitoring telemetry for ops but need to ensure it doesn't contain sensitive text. Can telemetry be scrubbing-first?
[11:59] Priya Shah: Yes, telemetry is scrubbed by default. We only include aggregate metrics and ID-level traces; full-text telemetry is optional and can be turned off.
[12:10] Marcus Liu: Any red flags from your side for us — things we should watch out for in the contract?
[12:16] Alex Turner: Check the data processing addendum for processor responsibilities, deletion SLAs, and cross-border fallback clauses. We'll propose language for strict residency and key control.
[12:28] Lena Park: Great. Can you also include an estimated unit cost for embeddings and generation for Dedicated so we can run a quick TCO?
[12:35] Alex Turner: We'll include sample TCO lines — tokens, embeddings, inference hours — and show delta between Hosted and Dedicated and rough ops assumptions.
[12:46] Marcus Liu: On legal timelines — we need to present to risk/compliance by April 15. Can you get doc pack before then?
[12:54] Alex Turner: Yes, we'll target April 1 for the compliance pack and pricing, then schedule the SE deep-dive early next week.
[13:05] Sofia Ramirez: One last concern — watermarking and provenance. We need to show auditors that outputs can be traced to generation events.
[13:12] Priya Shah: We provide generation IDs and signed metadata for each response; you can persist those in your logs for provenance.
[13:22] Ethan Cole: If we move forward, do you support a phased approach? Pilot -> limited production -> full production?
[13:28] Alex Turner: Absolutely; that's the normal path. Pilot in Dedicated, validate controls and perf, then reserve capacity and roll out routes.
[13:36] Marcus Liu: Ok, let's recap. Marcus: internal sign-off and share sanitized dataset. Alex/Redwood: send SOC2/HIPAA docs, GDPR mapping, Dedicated sizing/pricing, and schedule SE deep-dive.
[13:50] Alex Turner: Correct. I'll send the pack and price sheet by April 1. Priya will set up the SE deep-dive and benchmark plan. Ethan, if you can share the network diagram that'd help.
[14:02] Ethan Cole: Will do — I'll email the diagram and list of external integrations by Friday.
[14:08] Lena Park: Thanks everyone. Anything else?
[14:12] Sofia Ramirez: No, thanks. Looking forward to the docs.
[14:16] Alex Turner: Great, talk soon. Bye.
[14:20] [call ended]
